text: Hai Phong targets 13-13.5% economic growth in 2027

The northern port city of Hai Phong aims to achieve gross regional domestic product (GRDP) growth of 13-13.5% in 2027, exceeding the estimated 12.39% growth in 2026, according to the city's proposed socio-economic development plan.
Industry and construction are expected to grow by 15.5-16%, compared with an estimated 14.36% in 2026, while services are projected to expand by 11.5-12%, against 11.31%.
Agriculture, forestry and fisheries are targeted to grow by 2.4%, up from an estimated 2.3%.
Manufacturing, seaports, logistics, trade and services will remain key growth drivers.
The city targets a 16-16.5% increase in its industrial production index (IIP), compared with an estimated 15.2-15.5% in 2026.
Manufacturing is expected to account for 46% of GRDP, up from an estimated 44.41%.
Hai Phong also aims to increase export turnover to $61 billion in 2027, up from an estimated $55.6 billion in 2026.
Cargo throughput at its ports is targeted at 258 million tons, an increase of 19.8 million tons.
The city also aims to attract $4.5-5 billion in foreign investment in 2027, up from an estimated $4.2-4.3 billion in 2026.
Meanwhile, the digital economy is expected to account for 25.5% of GRDP, compared with an estimated 22.6% in 2026
The city expects to welcome 19 million tourist arrivals, including 2.1 million international visitors staying at local accommodation establishments.
